caption:
Security startup Straiker says a crime group called CyberCartel used AI agents built on Claude, Grok and Kimi to target more than 400 banks and payment firms in Latin America.
Claude agents planned the moves, Grok agents scouted targets, and the group got past safety rules by posing as security testers.
Anthropic cut off its access and xAI is investigating. Straiker's figures have not been independently verified.

Should AI companies answer for it when criminals misuse their models?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: GBHackers · Photo: Straiker
threads_text: A crime group reportedly ran Claude, Grok and Kimi agents as one team against more than 400 Latin American banks, with Claude planning and Grok scouting. They got past the guardrails by claiming to be security testers. Is pretending to be a red team too easy a way around AI safety rules?

paragraphs.text: Security startup Straiker said in a report published on October 21, 2026, that a financially motivated crime group it links to CyberCartel used AI agents built on several commercial models to target more than 400 banks, payment providers and other financial firms across Latin America. The models named in the report are Anthropic's Claude, xAI's Grok and Moonshot AI's Kimi, according to GBHackers and Infobae.

Straiker tracks the group as AiPT-67 and says it operated as Tr4nsHack Team under the name Hexagon Security Labs Mexico, which Infobae described as a suspected front. Straiker says CyberCartel has been active since 2012. The firm did not name the targeted institutions.
How the agents divided the work

Straiker calls the operation CARLIY0S and says it was built around PentAGI, an open-source framework for offensive security testing. According to GBHackers, Claude agents analyzed targets, weighed possible approaches and pulled decisions together, while agents running on Grok worked as miners that gathered information into a database the group called FinancialSoft. Kimi models also appeared in the workflow.

Digital Today, citing a report by The Information, said four agents running on Claude Opus and Sonnet models discussed the best attack methods, and a Claude model running inside the Cursor coding app acted as the commander that directed the overall work. Agents on Grok searched the web for information about targets.

The group framed its prompts as authorized security testing to get the models past their safety limits, according to GBHackers and Business Today. When Claude refused a task, Digital Today reported, the work was passed to smaller models such as Kimi, and when those refused as well, the operators switched to conventional attack code. Straiker also found automated browser activity and the use of residential proxy services.

Straiker said a snapshot of the FinancialSoft database taken on September 24, 2026, held 4,493 records, including 2,911 email addresses and 903 account numbers, along with passwords, API keys and other access material. Infobae reported that the findings also included data related to SPEI, the interbank electronic payment system run in Mexico.

Both GBHackers and Business Today stressed that the figure of more than 400 counts organizations that were targeted and does not show that each one was breached. GBHackers also noted that some model configuration entries Straiker found do not prove those models were actually used, and that the numbers are Straiker's findings rather than an independently verified tally of intrusions or losses.

According to Straiker, Anthropic revoked the compromised credential the group used to reach Claude, and Digital Today reported that Anthropic blocked CyberCartel after its own investigation. xAI was notified and is examining the activity tied to the Grok agents. Straiker was still trying to reach Moonshot AI, and no response from that company was reported.

The case shows how a refusal by one model does little when an operator can route the same task to another model or to ordinary code. Safety rules that depend on a single provider saying no are weaker when attackers spread the work across several providers, and a claim of authorized testing remains an easy cover story for misuse.
Watch whether xAI and Moonshot AI report what they found, and whether any Latin American bank or regulator confirms breaches linked to the campaign.
